20.t: Working with data: heating egg white
q: Estimate the temperature at which absorbance after 10 minutes reaches half its maximum.
Compare the effect of temperature after 10 and 30 minutes of heating.
Both are low at 40 °C and level off near 0.97 above 80 °C. Between 50 and 70 °C the 30-minute curve is higher: it is shifted about 8 °C to the left.
Explain why heating for longer increases denaturation at 60 °C but not at 90 °C.

At 60 °C only some molecules have enough energy to break their hydrogen bonds at any moment, so more unfold the longer they are heated. At 90 °C almost all are denatured within 10 minutes, so there is nothing left to change.
The largest error bars are at 60 and 70 °C. Suggest why.
This is the steepest part of the curve: a small difference in temperature or timing between tubes causes a large difference in absorbance.
Explain why the egg white stays cloudy when it cools down.
Denaturation is permanent here: the unfolded chains form new bonds with each other and clump together, so the original 3D shape cannot re-form.
